holidays.name: Singles' Day
holidays.description: The number 11/11 looks like four people standing alone, so the date has become a celebration of being single. People treat themselves to gifts, meet up with friends, and chase online bargains. It's now one of the biggest shopping days on Earth.
holidays.origin: Singles' Day is generally traced to Nanjing University students in China in the 1990s. They embraced the four 'bare sticks' of 11/11 as a playful anti-Valentine's celebration. Online retailers later turned it into a giant shopping festival.
holidays.funFact: Alibaba's 2009 Singles' Day sale launched with only 27 merchants. It has since grown into a global event that rings up tens of billions of dollars in sales.

holidays.name: National Sundae Day
holidays.description: A day to pile ice cream high in a bowl and bury it under hot fudge, whipped cream, sprinkles and a cherry on top. Build one yourself, or host a sundae bar and let everyone invent their own masterpiece.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance, and its origin is unclear. The sundae itself has a famously disputed past. Several American towns claim to have invented it in the late 1800s.
holidays.funFact: One popular legend says the sundae was created to get around old 'blue laws' that banned selling ice cream sodas on Sundays. The spelling 'sundae' supposedly avoided offending anyone.

holidays.name: Origami Day
holidays.description: Grab a square of paper and start folding. Cranes, frogs, boats and boxes all count. It celebrates the Japanese art of paper folding, which turns a flat sheet into something surprising without scissors or glue.
holidays.origin: Origami Day is an observance of the traditional Japanese paper-folding art. It is marked on November 11 each year by paper-folding fans and crafters.
holidays.funFact: Tradition holds that folding 1,000 paper cranes, called senbazuru, earns you a wish. Many people hang the strings of cranes as symbols of hope and peace.
